item.title: Gymnasium-Robotics Library Releases with Reinforcement Learning Robotic Environments
item.description:
Gymnasium-Robotics Library Releases with Reinforcement Learning Robotic Environments

The Gymnasium-Robotics library has been released, offering a collection of Reinforcement Learning robotic environments built on the Gymnasium API and powered by the MuJoCo physics engine. Users can install environments via pip, with support for both the maintained MuJoCo Python bindings and legacy mujoco-py versions through optional extras. The package is officially supported on Linux and macOS, with community contributions welcomed for Windows compatibility.

🧩 Available Environments

  • Fetch Environments: 7-degree-of-freedom robot arm for tasks including Reach, Push, Slide, and Pick and Place
  • Shadow Dexterous Hand Environments: 24-degree-of-freedom anthropomorphic hand for object manipulation with cube, egg-object, or pen
  • Maze Environments: Navigation tasks using 2-DoF force-controlled ball or Ant agent, with varying maze complexity
  • Adroit Arm Environments: Shadow Dexterous Hand with additional arm degrees of freedom for hammering, door opening, pen twirling, and ball manipulation
  • Franka Kitchen Environments: 9-DoF Franka robot arm in a kitchen setting for multitask interaction scenarios
  • MaMuJoCo: Multi-agent factorizations using pettingzoo.ParallelEnv API
  • D4RL Environments: Now available with refactored action/observation spaces

⚙️ API and Features

The environments extend the core Gymnasium API by inheriting from GoalEnv class, which enforces:

  • Dictionary observation space containing three required keys
  • Exposed reward, terminated, and truncated signals for flexible goal re-computation
  • Compatibility with Hindsight Experience Replay (HER) algorithms

Some environment variations include data from 92 touch sensors in the observation space.

#ReinforcementLearning #Robotics #MuJoCo #Gymnasium #RLENvironments

Source: Farama-Foundation/Gymnasium-Robotics

item.title: Datawhale China Releases Alpha Version of Embodied AI Learning Platform with Online Simulation
item.description:
Datawhale China Releases Alpha Version of Embodied AI Learning Platform with Online Simulation

Datawhale China has launched an alpha internal test version of “Dive into Embodied AI” (具身智能), a comprehensive learning platform for embodied intelligent robot development. The platform covers the full “decision—control—perception” pipeline using reinforcement learning, world models, and VLA (Vision-Language-Action) methods across simulation environments, controllers, motion planning, and perception systems.

🔍 Overview

The platform is structured into four main sections:

  • Embodied Introduction (具身导论): Field overview with curated papers, datasets, open-source projects, and tools
  • Theoretical Foundation (理论基础): Core principles and concepts
  • Project Practice (项目实战): Hands-on projects organized by AMD Zone, Simulation Practice, and Real Machine Practice
  • Online Simulation (在线仿真): Interactive browser-based simulation environment

The release is labeled as an alpha internal test version, currently undergoing migration and restructuring with some chapters as placeholder pages. Users are encouraged to submit issues for feedback.

🧩 How it works

Online Simulation Features

The simulation environment (accessible at https://datawhalechina.github.io/dive-into-embodied-ai/simulation) provides:

  • Two modes: game-style free manipulation and policy demonstration
  • Pre-loaded policies:
    • Go2 and Pupper v3 PPO walking policies
    • Quaddle periodic gait comparison
    • MicroDuck head and full-body joint free manipulation (walking weights not yet available)
  • Controls: keyboard and on-screen directional buttons, pause, reset, slow simulation, camera follow
  • Go2 displays with simplified appearance using original collision model

Curriculum Structure

Embodied Introduction (7 chapters):

  1. What is Embodied AI — definition, perception-decision-action loop, body importance
  2. Development History — rule programming, model control, deep RL, and large model eras
  3. Robot Skills — tasks, grasping, manipulation, locomotion, navigation
  4. Embodied Carriers — humanoid, robotic arms, wheeled, quadruped, mobile manipulation, simulation bodies
  5. Core Challenges — data, sim-to-real, generalization, real-time, safety, evaluation
  6. Tech Stack — VLM, VLA, world models, manipulation, control, navigation modules
  7. Career Roles — brain algorithms, cerebellum algorithms, perception/navigation, engineering platforms, hardware

Project Practice Categories:

Category Projects
AMD Zone AUP Learning Cloud (Ryzen AI APU, ROCm, JupyterHub, Code Server); MicroDuck RL on AMD ROCm (R9700, ROCm MuJoCo Warp, dynamic contact regression, bipedal PPO); Pupper Quadruped on AMD (RL locomotion policies, VLA experiments)
Simulation Practice Build Quadruped from Scratch (MuJoCo, PD, kinematics, policy training, language control, perception); Petoi Quaddle Servo Walking (official URDF, alternating gait, contact verification, infinite checkerboard); MicroDuck RL (mjlab + MuJoCo Warp, GPU parallel PPO, bipedal gait); MuJoCo Arm with DDPG; ACT Bimanual Manipulation (ACT + ALOHA training, evaluation, reproduction)
Real Machine Practice LeRobot Chinese Course (Units 0-2: robot learning, datasets, toolchain, classic robotics); SO-101 + LeRobot Real Machine Tutorial (hardware connection, safety testing, action replay)

🚀 Availability

  • Platform language support: Chinese, English, Italian
  • Alpha version — active migration and restructuring in progress
  • Some chapters are placeholder pages
  • Model library integration planned (see simulation/README.md)
  • Tutorial and interactive pages include “Copy as Markdown” with Markdown preview dropdown

💡 Why it matters

This platform provides an end-to-end educational resource bridging theory and practice for embodied AI development, with particular emphasis on hardware-accessible projects (AMD ROCm support, real robot tutorials) and interactive browser-based simulation for immediate experimentation without local GPU setup.

#EmbodiedAI #Robotics #ReinforcementLearning #VLA #MuJoCo #Datawhale

Source: datawhalechina/dive-into-embodied-ai

item.title: Scaling MuJoCo Simulations to GPU with MuJoCo Warp
item.description:
Scaling MuJoCo Simulations to GPU with MuJoCo Warp

As part of the State of Simulation for Physical AI series, MuJoCo Warp (MJWarp) has been introduced to move compatible MuJoCo models into a GPU-scale regime. This development enables the transition of workflows, such as an SO-101 follower arm, from standard MuJoCo to as many as 2,048 parallel environments.

🧩 How it works

MJWarp is an implementation of MuJoCo’s physics pipeline that places the model and a batch of independent states on NVIDIA GPUs. The process functions as follows:

  • Model Handling: MuJoCo loads and compiles the MJCF model.
  • Physics Execution: MJWarp implements the physics using NVIDIA Warp, which compiles CUDA kernels to advance simulation states on NVIDIA GPUs.
  • Execution: A single call to mjw.step advances the simulation.

⚙️ Key details

MJWarp is built on NVIDIA Warp, a Python framework for writing high-performance, GPU-accelerated kernels.

Feature Description
Kernel Language A performance-oriented subset of Python; ordinary Python handles configuration, allocation, and launch orchestration.
Compilation Statically typed kernels are compiled for CPU or CUDA execution; the first launch builds and caches a native module for later reuse.
Scaling One logical thread handles one point, allowing code to scale from two points to millions.
Differentiability A wp.Tape records forward kernel launches and replays adjoints in reverse via backward().
Determinism Opt-in deterministic modes (introduced in Warp 1.15) provide reproducible ordering for validation and regression tests by managing GPU atomics.

💡 Why it matters

While MuJoCo is naturally suited for developing and inspecting one or a few CPU worlds, MJWarp allows for massive parallelism. In this context, a “world” is one independent copy of a scene and its state—for example, one world may feature an SO-101 arm reaching for a cube while another features the same arm in a different pose.

🚀 Availability

Users can install Warp via pip install warp-lang (version 1.15 or higher is required for GPU determinism). Tutorial notebooks and the python -m warp.examples.browse command are also available.

#MuJoCo #NVIDIAWarp #GPU #Robotics #Simulation

Source: How to Use NVIDIA Warp and MjWarp to Accelerate Robotics Simulation and Learning Workflows
